summary: Backend-only testing of NEW Smart Multi-Pharmacy Price Optimization feature. Created /app/backend/tests/test_optimize.py with 13 pytest cases covering (a) new supplier product fields (quantity, delivery_time, supplier_phone auto-population from supplier profile, marketplace exposes them) and (b) POST /api/orders/optimize: role enforcement (403 supplier / 401 no-token), full response shape (unavailable/per_item/single_supplier/smart_split/summary), per-item cheapest-ignoring-qty plan, single-supplier filtering (only suppliers with ALL items), smart-split across suppliers when qty insufficient (10@900 + 20@1000 for 30 units), qty=0 treated as unlimited, substring matching both directions ('PANA' <-> 'PANA EXTRA'), unavailable items list, and summary.max_savings = most_expensive - cheapest. All 13/13 new tests pass + 29/29 prior tests still pass = 42/42 total (100%).

minor.issue: Substring matching is double-sided (q in n OR n in q). A query 'paracetamol' will match an unrelated supplier product literally named 'amol'. Could cause false-positive matches in production when product names are short.

OptimizeRequest.items has no minimum-length validation - empty basket returns {unavailable:[], per_item:{plan:[],total:0}, single_supplier:{options:[],best:null}, smart_split:{groups:[],items_summary:[]}, summary:{cheapest_total:0,most_expensive_total:0,max_savings:0}} (200 OK). Probably acceptable but worth a 400.
summary.cheapest_total / most_expensive_total are NOT rounded to 2dp like max_savings; minor inconsistency only.
No validation that price>=0 or quantity>=0; negative values are accepted and would distort optimize results.
smart_split.savings_vs_max is rounded but per_item.total and smart_split.total are floats that may carry FP noise (e.g., 29000.0 fine, but mixed-currency cases could see 0.30000000004).

action_items: Optional: Tighten substring matching (e.g., word-boundary or token-overlap) to avoid false matches when product names are short.
Optional: Add Pydantic min_length=1 validator on OptimizeRequest.items and reject empty baskets with 400.
Optional: Add ge=0 constraint to SupplierProductCreate.price and quantity.
Optional: Round summary.cheapest_total / most_expensive_total to 2dp for consistency.
critical_code_review_comments: Algorithm in /api/orders/optimize loads ALL supplier_products into memory (find({}).to_list(5000)) and iterates per requested item - O(items * products). Fine at current scale; consider an indexed text search or projection if marketplace grows large.
qty=0 'unlimited' semantics is non-obvious - documented in docstring is good, but consider an explicit field like 'unlimited: bool' to avoid confusion with literally-out-of-stock.
Substring-based name matching is fragile in Arabic where diacritics/normalization vary; recommend Unicode normalization (NFKC) and stripping tashkeel before compare.
Optimize endpoint correctly enforces pharmacy-only role. supplier_phone is correctly auto-populated server-side (not trusted from client). MongoDB _id is excluded everywhere.
seed_data_creation: Each module-scoped fixture run registers 3 fresh suppliers with phones derived from current timestamp (TEST_SUPPA_/TEST_SUPPB_/TEST_SUPPC_) and creates 5 supplier products with unique English names (PANAZQX<RUN>, ASPIZQX<RUN>, PANAZQX<RUN>EXTRA) so that substring matching does not collide with the existing seeded marketplace data ('بنادول', 'فيتامين سي', 'اموكسيسيلين'). All 5 test products are deleted at fixture teardown. Pre-seeded pharmacy 07700000001/pass123 and seeded marketplace data are not modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All optimize behavior verified end-to-end with deterministic prices/qty: per_item cheapest=900 ignores qty, single_supplier excludes suppliers missing any basket item, smart_split correctly splits 30 units = 10@900(A) + 20@1000(B), qty=0 treated as unlimited fills remaining 40 units in test, groups sorted by total desc, substring match works both directions, summary.max_savings == round(most_expensive - cheapest, 2). All response keys (unavailable/per_item/single_supplier/smart_split/summary) present with documented shape. Re-run: pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v. IMPORTANT: tests use English unique tokens (ZQX<timestamp>) instead of Arabic to avoid false substring hits with seeded marketplace data - keep this convention if extending tests.
rca_of_issue: No bugs found in the new feature. During test development I initially used Arabic names (بنادول_<RUN>) which collided with the already-seeded marketplace product 'بنادول' via the bidirectional substring match logic, masking my newly-created supplier products. Switched to unique English tokens to make assertions deterministic. This collision confirmed the substring-matching minor concern above (q-in-n OR n-in-q), which is reported as a non-blocking minor issue to consider hardening.
